[The top 100 ranked color names from the xkcd color survey by hue, lightness and saturation]{.subtitle} <br> (sized by rank)

```{python} 
#setup -------------------------------

#load libraries
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import colorsys
import math

#load data
df = pd.read_csv("color_ranks.csv")

#convert hex into rgb and hls color space
df["rgb"] = [tuple(int(hex.lstrip('#')[i:i+2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4)) for hex in df["hex"]]
df["rgb_n"] =[[round(rgb[0]/255,4), round(rgb[1]/255,4), round(rgb[2]/255,4)] for rgb in df["rgb"]]
df["hls_n"] = [colorsys.rgb_to_hls(rgb[0], rgb[1], rgb[2]) for rgb in df["rgb_n"]]
df["hls_n"] = [ [round(i[0] ,4), round(i[1],4), round(i[2],4)] for i in df["hls_n"]]
df["hls"] = [ [int(i[0]*360), int(i[1]*100), int(i[2]*100)] for i in df["hls_n"]]
```

```{python}
df_to_plot = df.head(100)

#explore colors in 3D space
hue = list(df_to_plot["hls"].str[0])
light = list(df_to_plot["hls"].str[1])
sat = list(df_to_plot["hls"].str[2])
size = [(len(df_to_plot)-i *0.1) for i in df_to_plot["rank"]]
size = [math.sqrt(math.sqrt(len(df_to_plot)-i))**3 *1.3 for i in df_to_plot.index]

fig = go.Figure()
fig = px.scatter_3d(df_to_plot, x=hue, y=sat, z=light, custom_data=['color', 'rank']).update_traces(
                        marker=dict(color=df_to_plot["hex"]),
                        marker_size=size,
                        hovertemplate =
                        "<b>%{customdata[0]}</b><br>" +
                        "Rank: %{customdata[1]}<br><br>")
                    
fig = fig.update_layout(scene = dict(
                      xaxis=dict(title=dict(text='Hue') ),
                      yaxis=dict(title=dict( text='Saturation')),
                      zaxis=dict(title=dict(text='Lightness')),
                    ), 
                      autosize=False,
                      width=750,
                      height=450,
                      template="plotly_white",
                      margin=dict(l=0,r=0,t=0,b=0), scene_camera=dict(eye=dict(x=2, y=2.0, z=0.75))
        )

fig.show()
```
